_note: Original sample questions for M1. Audio and images are generated later (M2/M3); audio_script holds the text to be spoken.

questions.instructions: Read the text out loud, clearly and at a natural speed.

content.text: Many cities now plant trees along busy roads. The trees give shade in summer, reduce noise from traffic and make the streets more pleasant for people who walk to work.

answer.reference_text: Many cities now plant trees along busy roads. The trees give shade in summer, reduce noise from traffic and make the streets more pleasant for people who walk to work.

questions.explanation: Read in phrases, not word by word. Pause briefly at commas and full stops.
questions.learning_objective: Read a short factual text aloud with clear pronunciation and natural phrasing.

questions.instructions: Read the text out loud, clearly and at a natural speed.

content.text: Researchers studying sleep have found that teenagers naturally fall asleep later than adults. As a result, some schools have moved their start time to later in the morning, and early reports suggest that attendance has improved.

answer.reference_text: Researchers studying sleep have found that teenagers naturally fall asleep later than adults. As a result, some schools have moved their start time to later in the morning, and early reports suggest that attendance has improved.

questions.explanation: Stress the content words (researchers, teenagers, later, attendance) and keep a steady pace.
questions.learning_objective: Read a longer academic text with correct word stress.

answer.reference_text: The library closes at six on Fridays.

questions.explanation: Listen for meaning, not single words. Remember the sentence as one idea.
questions.learning_objective: Hold a short sentence in memory and repeat it accurately.

questions.instructions: Look at the picture. Describe the main things it shows and what they mean.

image.title: Books borrowed per month at a town library

answer.model_answer: The bar chart shows how many books a town library lent each month from January to April. Borrowing dipped slightly from 420 in January to 380 in February, then rose steadily to a peak of 600 in April. Overall, the library became busier during spring.

questions.explanation: Say what the image is, give the highest and lowest values, describe the trend, then give a conclusion.
questions.learning_objective: Describe a simple bar chart using trend language.

questions.instructions: Look at the picture. Describe the main things it shows and what they mean.

image.title: How students travel to a college

answer.model_answer: The pie chart shows how students get to a college. The bus is the most common choice at forty percent, followed by walking at a quarter. Twenty percent cycle, and only fifteen percent travel by car. In short, most students use low-cost or active travel.

questions.explanation: Compare the parts: biggest, smallest and any similar values.
questions.learning_objective: Describe proportions in a pie chart.

questions.instructions: Listen to the talk, then tell it again in your own words.

content.audio_script: Today I want to talk about honeybees and why farmers care about them. Bees carry pollen from flower to flower, and this allows many fruit and vegetable plants to produce food. In some regions, bee numbers have fallen because of disease, loss of wild flowers and certain pesticides. Some farmers now plant strips of wild flowers beside their fields to give bees food and shelter.

answer.model_answer: The lecture explained that bees are important to farmers because they pollinate many food crops. Bee numbers have dropped in some places because of disease, fewer wild flowers and pesticides. To help, some farmers grow wild flower strips next to their fields.

questions.explanation: Note the topic, two or three main points and the conclusion. Use your own words.
questions.learning_objective: Retell the main ideas of a short lecture.

questions.instructions: Listen to the talk, then tell it again in your own words.

content.audio_script: The idea of a four-day working week has moved from theory to real trials. In several trials, staff kept the same pay but worked one day less. Many companies reported similar output, while employees described less stress and better sleep. Critics argue that the results may not apply to jobs such as hospital care, where someone must always be present.

answer.model_answer: The speaker discussed trials of a four-day working week with no cut in pay. Many firms kept the same output and workers reported lower stress and better sleep. However, critics say the model may not suit jobs like hospital work that need constant cover.

questions.explanation: Include the contrast at the end: the benefits and the criticism.
questions.learning_objective: Retell a lecture that includes a counter-argument.
key_points: may not suit jobs needing constant cover

questions.instructions: Listen to the discussion, then say what the main points were in your own words.

audio_script.speaker: Amira
audio_script.text: I think the university should keep the library open all night during exams.

audio_script.speaker: Ben
audio_script.text: That sounds good, but who pays for the extra staff and security?

audio_script.speaker: Chen
audio_script.text: Maybe we could open just one floor overnight, with self-service machines, to keep costs down.

answer.model_answer: The students discussed opening the library all night during exams. Amira supported the idea, Ben worried about the cost of staff and security, and Chen suggested a compromise of opening one self-service floor overnight.

questions.explanation: Name each speaker's position and the final suggestion.
questions.learning_objective: Summarize different opinions in a short discussion.
key_points: proposal: open library overnight in exams
concern: cost of staff and security

questions.instructions: Listen to the discussion, then say what the main points were in your own words.

audio_script.speaker: Dana
audio_script.text: Our group project should use online meetings, because we all live far apart.

audio_script.speaker: Eli
audio_script.text: Online is convenient, but last time people turned their cameras off and nobody spoke.

audio_script.speaker: Farah
audio_script.text: Then let's meet online each week but set a short agenda and give everyone a task to report on.

answer.model_answer: The group talked about how to meet for their project. Dana preferred online meetings because members live far apart. Eli agreed they are convenient but said people did not take part last time. Farah proposed weekly online meetings with an agenda and a task for each person.

questions.explanation: Show how the ideas build on each other to reach a solution.
questions.learning_objective: Summarize a discussion that reaches a solution.
key_points: solution: agenda and tasks for everyone

questions.instructions: Read and listen to the situation, then say what you would say in it.

content.situation: You borrowed a classmate's notes for a week, but you spilled coffee on one page. You are going to return the notes now. What do you say to your classmate?

answer.model_answer: Hi Jamie, thank you so much for lending me your notes. I'm really sorry, but I spilled some coffee on page four. I've copied that page out neatly for you, and I'm happy to buy you a coffee to say sorry.

questions.explanation: Thank the person, explain the problem honestly, apologise and offer a solution.
questions.learning_objective: Apologise politely and offer a solution.

questions.instructions: Read and listen to the situation, then say what you would say in it.

content.situation: Your manager has asked you to work this Saturday, but you have already booked a train ticket to visit your family. What do you say to your manager?

answer.model_answer: Thanks for thinking of me for Saturday. Unfortunately, I've already booked a train to visit my family that day, so I can't come in. Could I help by staying late on Thursday or Friday, or by finishing part of the work from home before I leave?

questions.explanation: Decline politely, give a reason and offer an alternative.
questions.learning_objective: Decline a request politely in a work setting.

questions.instructions: Read the passage, then sum up its main idea in one sentence.

content.passage: Community gardens are spaces where neighbours grow vegetables and flowers together on shared land. Supporters say they improve access to fresh food, especially in areas with few shops. They also bring people of different ages and backgrounds together, which can reduce loneliness. However, gardens often depend on volunteers and temporary agreements with landowners, so many struggle to survive for more than a few years.

answer.model_answer: Community gardens improve access to fresh food and bring neighbours together, but their reliance on volunteers and temporary land agreements often makes them hard to sustain.

questions.explanation: Combine the main benefit and the main problem in one sentence with a linking word such as "but".
questions.learning_objective: Write a one-sentence summary that links ideas.
key_points: depend on volunteers and temporary land

questions.instructions: Read the passage, then sum up its main idea in one sentence.

content.passage: Electric scooters for hire have spread quickly through many cities. They offer a cheap and fast way to make short trips without a car. Yet city councils have raised concerns about riders using pavements, scooters left blocking paths, and injuries among inexperienced users. In response, some cities now require parking zones, speed limits in busy areas and helmets for younger riders.

answer.model_answer: Although hire e-scooters provide cheap, fast short trips, safety and obstruction concerns have led some cities to introduce parking zones, speed limits and helmet rules.

questions.explanation: Use "although" to show the contrast, then give the response.
questions.learning_objective: Summarize a problem-solution text in one sentence.
key_points: rules: parking zones, speed limits, helmets
